Title: GET /posts returns status 200 and 100 posts
Expected Result: Status 200, content type application/json, the response time is under 5 seconds and the list has 100 posts.

Title: GET /posts/1 matches the post JSON schema
Steps: 1. Send GET /posts/1. 2. Validate the body against the post schema.
Expected Result: Status 200. The body is valid against the schema, id is 1 and userId is 1.

Title: GET /posts?userId=1 returns 10 posts that all belong to user 1
Expected Result: Status 200. 10 posts are returned and every post has userId 1.

Title: GET /posts/1/comments returns 5 comments of post 1 with valid emails
Expected Result: Status 200. 5 comments are returned, every comment has postId 1 and every email contains "@".

Title: POST /posts creates a post and returns status 201 with the new id 101
Test Data: title "QA demo", body "created by REST Assured", userId 7
Steps: 1. Send POST /posts with the JSON body.
Expected Result: Status 201. The answer repeats title "QA demo" and userId 7 and has the new id 101.

Title: PUT /posts/1 replaces the post and returns status 200
Steps: 1. Send PUT /posts/1 with the JSON body.
Expected Result: Status 200 and the title in the answer is "updated".

Title: PATCH /posts/1 changes only the title and returns status 200
Steps: 1. Send PATCH /posts/1 with the JSON body {"title": "patched"}.
Expected Result: Status 200. The title is "patched" and the id is still 1.
